changes.reason: No sensor is read. The function has two parts. (1) It clears parameter_block_uploaded and loads a flash parameter block. When both marker words 0x55B2 and 0x75B2 hold 0xA1A1, it loads block 1 and clears the RAM copy of the marker at 0x806548. Otherwise it picks the newest complete block from the save start / complete counts and the odd / even sum of the two start counts (cm550_loadParameterBlock1FromFlash / cm550_loadParameterBlock2FromFlash), with the other block as fallback. When no block loaded, it sets status word 0 bit 0x1000 (all power-down data lost) and its first-occurrence bit. engine_startup_inhibit_true_false = 1 while that bit is set, confirmed (0x806abc bit 0x1000) and 0x808484 = 0. (2) It does the start-up power-down bookkeeping that CM848 does inline in cm848_applicationMain, in the same order. If power_cycle_sequence_number_cal = completed_power_down_sequence_number_cal: consecutive count <- 0, completed count +1, clear bit 0x800. Otherwise: consecutive count +1, incomplete count +1, and bit 0x800 is set when the consecutive count is above 0x808480. Last: sequence number <- completed + incomplete. Each write goes through cm550_parameterCircularBufferWrite and waits up to 5000 passes of 500 timebase ticks (CM848: 5000 passes), with interrupts enabled (andi #0xf1ff,sr) around the wait. mc68k_applicationMain calls it once, right before its inline flash_write_failure_flag_cal and 0x803fda checks; that is CM848's order. Prefix cm550_: no CM848 function does this, because the CM848 bookkeeping is inline code. The CM848 inline code also sets fault_detected_cal.power_off_without_ignition_off_error and high_idle_override_flag, which this function does not, so it is a counterpart, not a twin. It accesses no MC68336 module register (only SR for the interrupt mask, as cm550_savePowerDownDataToFlashBank does) and nothing VP44-related.

changes.reason: This is the boot ROM's software-restart entry: a point inside the body of mc68k_hardwareInitAndStartup that has its own function row, like cm550_restartApplicationWithoutReset (0x28978) inside mc68k_applicationMain. How it is reached: (a) restartThroughBootRom (0x1192a, twin of CM848 0x216fc) masks interrupts, sets SP to 0x811000, loads the long at ROM 0x8 and jumps to it. (b) The cold path falls into it: reset PC 0x1e (SIM / clock / chip selects) -> jsr 0x3a94, which writes the chip select 2 device (0xffd008 = 0x40, 0xffd00e = 0x80), waits for the chip select 2 input bit 0 (mc68k_waitForChipSelect2InputBit0High), sets port E bit 3, and then runs on into 0x3abe. So the warm entry skips exactly those steps. What it does from 0x3abe: stops the QSPI (SPSR &0x7f, SPCR1 &0x7fff, SPCR2 &0x7fff / &0xfff0); clears QILR / SCCR1, PICR / PITR, TPU_CIER and the QADC registers; resets and configures CTM4 (BIUMCR 0x1601, CPCR 8, MCSM11SIC 4, FCSM12SIC 0x104); sets QSMCR 5 / QILR 0x13 / QIVR 0x50; clears RAM (cm550_ramClearWithWatchdog). Then it starts the Huffman-decompressed RAM kernel at 0x80339e when mc68k_portPinTestSequence2 returns 1 or the serial EEPROM signature is not 0x600d. Otherwise it starts the application through the long at 0x8062 when the 0x8000 header is 0x98765432 / 0x98765433 (dump: 0x98765432 -> 0x1dbee), or else through the long at 0x20000. mc68k_ because it writes MC68336 module registers. Counterpart, not a twin, of CM848 mpc555_hardwareInitialization (0x2694). Matches: the QSPI stop constants, the 0x600d EEPROM check, a four-pin QADC strap test, the kernel-or-application ending, and a pointer word right after the reset vector (CM550 0x8 / CM848 0x104) that the twin restartThroughBootRom jumps through. Differences: CM848 adds BR0-3 / OR0-3 / SIUMCR, the MIOS counter set-up, the TPU module stop and the flash2 identification. CM550 adds PICR / PITR, the CTM4 block and QSMCR / QILR / QIVR. CM550 tests the pins before it reads the EEPROM; CM848 reads the EEPROM first. CM550 selects the program by the 0x8000 signature and 0x8062; CM848 jumps through flash_operational_code_entry_pointer. CM848's is a whole function with three call sites; CM550's is a mid-body entry. This follows the precedent of mc68k_waitForChipSelect2InputBit0High / mc68k_checkSerialEepromSignature, which have 'same pattern as CM848' notes and kept mc68k_.

The output image of the SIM Port E pins, and an output request byte. It is e2m 000E +2A, byte 2 (outputs 16-23) of the 6-byte output image array 0x80bcf6-0x80bcfb. mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler writes it to SIM_PORTE0 with bit 5 inverted. Each writer sets or clears its bit only while that output's override slot (0x80bd1a + output number) is 0, then calls the strobe handler. The old name is the e2m text of one bit only. Bits: (mask 0x02) boot block programming enable (SSBBPGEA), set only around the boot block erase / program. (mask 0x04) flash programming enable (SSVTEA 'bit which allows the processor to enable flash programming'), on from the start of the power-down saves to their end, around every flash erase / program (parameter blocks 0x4000 / 0x6000 and the boot block). (mask 0x08) the ECM power hold, MEDIUM confidence by role: the boot block sets this pin first after reset, the application main sets it, and the power-down clears it after the saves and sets it again if the ECM is still running or the key comes back. Those are the steps CM848's cm848_runPowerDownSequence runs on logical output 27. (mask 0x10) set at the output start-up and cleared just before restartThroughBootRom jumps into the boot ROM; what it drives is not proven. (mask 0x20) driven inverted at the pin. Typed byte, not a bitfield struct (CM550 has none yet).
